title: Taiwanese Cultural Society at Stanford University
content_html:
The Taiwanese Cultural Society at Stanford University (TCS) is an undergraduate student organization that celebrates and promotes Taiwanese culture at Stanford and in the greater San Francisco Bay Area. The organization was formerly known as the “Taiwan Club” until 1995, when it was renamed the Taiwanese Cultural Society. It is housed within Stanford’s Asian American Activities Center (A³C) and is a member of both Stanford’s Asian American Student Association (AASA) and the Intercollegiate Taiwanese American Students Association (ITASA).

TCS describes itself as serving a diverse membership connected by a shared interest in Taiwanese culture and Taiwanese American identity. Its programming includes the annual Stanford Night Market — a large-scale public event featuring performances, food stalls, and games emulating the atmosphere of Taiwanese night markets — as well as a yearly “Taste of Taiwan” food event, cooking nights, movie screenings, quarterly retreats, study breaks, and ITASA inter-school mixers and conferences.

Through its affiliation with ITASA, TCS connects with Taiwanese American student groups at other universities across the West Coast and nationally, participating in leadership workshops and the annual ITASA West Coast Conference. The organization’s website copyright footer dates to 2005, indicating a sustained web presence of at least two decades.
